items.back: Let total work = LCM of the given days, so each rate is a whole number of units/day. Combined rate = sum of unit rates.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Efficiency and Work

items.front: A alone a days, B alone b days — together in how many days?
items.back: Together time = ab/(a+b) = 1/(1/a+1/b). Never add the days.

items.front: 'A is k times as efficient as B' — days relation?
items.back: Rate ratio A:B = k:1, so the days ratio is 1:k (the faster one takes fewer days). Wages follow efficiency.

items.front: Man-days rule for the same job?
items.back: M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂. More men or hours means fewer days; include W when the job size changes.
Convert all worker types to one unit via the given relation (e.g. 2 men = 3 women), THEN apply worker-days = workers × days.
Inlet rate is + (fill), outlet/leak is − (empty). Fill time = 1 ÷ net rate; tank fills only if net rate > 0.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Pipes and Cistern

items.front: Speed conversions and average speed for equal distances?
items.back: km/h → m/s ×5/18; m/s → km/h ×18/5. Average speed (equal distances) = 2xy/(x+y) (harmonic mean).

items.front: Relative speed — same vs opposite direction?
items.back: Same direction: difference of speeds. Opposite: sum of speeds. Used for overtaking, meeting and chase problems.
items.examPoint: Relative speed — same vs opposite direction

items.front: Train crossing distances — pole, platform, another train?
items.back: Pole/person: train length ÷ v. Platform: (L+P) ÷ v. Another train: (L₁+L₂) ÷ relative speed.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Problem on Train

items.front: Boats & streams — down/upstream and recovering speeds?
items.back: Downstream = B+S, Upstream = B−S. B = (down+up)/2, S = (down−up)/2.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Boat and Stream

items.front: 'A beats B by d metres' in an L-metre race — speed ratio?
items.back: In equal time A runs L while B runs (L−d), so the speed ratio = L : (L−d). A 'start of x m' means B runs (L−x).
